issues.description: Module-level monkey-patch of genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE violates the SDK's abstraction boundary
issues.detail: Reaching into a vendored library's private underscore-prefixed module to mutate a global at import time breaks the contract Google publishes for google-genai. Any caller that imports pipecat.services.google.llm silently re-tunes the shared SDK for the whole process, affecting unrelated Gemini clients. The comment even calls it a 'temporary hack' — the right ADT move is to construct a configured HttpOptions/client locally, or open an upstream issue, not to mutate private state of someone else's module.

issues.description: Image-model branch silently violates the LLM service's output contract by emitting OutputImageRawFrame with unspecified semantics
issues.detail: GoogleLLMService's supertype contract is text+tool-call streaming. Adding a branch that pushes OutputImageRawFrame mid-stream strengthens what downstream pipelines must accept without amending the documented postcondition. Any consumer written against the LLM service interface may not handle image frames. State the contract: which subtypes/models produce images, and what frame ordering guarantees hold relative to LLMTextFrame and aggregator boundaries.

issues.description: Image decoding assumes RGB format unconditionally, leaking PIL implementation through the frame contract
issues.detail: Pillow returns images in whatever mode the source encodes (RGBA, P, L for PNG). The code passes image.tobytes() with format='RGB' without calling image.convert('RGB'), so size and byte-length will disagree for non-RGB returns and downstream renderers will read garbled pixels. Either convert explicitly to honor the declared format, or propagate image.mode as the frame's format.

issues.description: Default model change from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash is a silent behavioral contract change for existing callers
issues.detail: Callers who relied on the default got different latency, pricing, and thinking-budget behavior on upgrade. The CHANGELOG notes it, but the constructor signature gives no deprecation path. For a long-lived multi-team library this should at minimum be called out as a breaking default and ideally staged, since the postcondition 'which model you get when you pass nothing' changed.

issues.description: Image-model detection by substring 'image' in model name is a fragile, undocumented predicate
issues.detail: _maybe_unset_thinking_budget now gates on 'image' in self._model_name. This couples a behavioral invariant (no thinking budget) to a naming convention Google controls. A future model named e.g. 'gemini-3-vision' would silently regress. Extract a small predicate is_image_generation_model() with the rule documented, so the contract is named and testable.

review.summary: The feature adds a useful capability but introduces three contract problems worth fixing before merge. The most serious is the module-import-time mutation of a private attribute on google-genai's internal client — a textbook leaky abstraction and a process-global side effect of importing pipecat.services.google.llm. Second, emitting OutputImageRawFrame from inside GoogleLLMService extends the service's postcondition without restating it; downstream consumers wired against the prior contract may not handle image frames, and the PIL mode/format mismatch will produce broken pixels for non-RGB returns. Smaller items: the default-model change is a silent behavior shift for existing callers, and substring-matching 'image' in the model name encodes a Google naming convention as an invariant. The right fix in each case is to name the contract: configure the SDK through its public surface, document which model classes produce which frame types, and convert images to a declared mode explicitly.
